name: Learn common airport and travel procedures
blurb: Knowing the process — check-in, security rules, immigration, connections, what to do when things go wrong — turns air travel from stressful to routine.
steps: Learn the timeline: online check-in, bag drop cutoffs, security queue estimates and the gate closing time, which is much earlier than departure.
Learn the security rules for liquids, electronics and batteries, and pack so nothing needs to come out at the last moment.
Learn the difference between transit, transfer and re-entry, and when you must collect and re-check bags on a connection.
Learn your rights when things go wrong — delay and cancellation compensation rules differ by region and are often unclaimed.
Learn to read a boarding pass fully: sequence number, zone, gate, and the codes that indicate a security selection or standby.
Build a repeatable routine: same pockets, same documents, same order, every trip.
tips: Never put medication, keys, documents or electronics in checked luggage.
A separated ticket connection is your risk if the first flight is late. A single ticket is the airline’s.
Know the minimum connection time for your transfer airport.
proof: You handle a multi-leg international trip, including a delay, without confusion or missed steps.
